candidates.summary: chromeShot's only success test is that a non-empty file sits at the destination, so a browser run that wrote nothing passes on a file an earlier run left there
candidates.failure_scenario: chromeShot never removes dst before launching the browser and never checks that the file it stats is new or is a PNG. Run gnopreview twice into the same -out (the README's local flow) and let the second browser run exit 0 without writing — `chromeShot("/bin/true", url, dst)` over a 22-byte file returns nil — and the previous run's image is published as this pull request's screenshot with no line on stderr.
candidates.verify_by: go test -run TestChromeShotFalseSuccess/stale_file ./... in misc/gnopreview with the artifact test: expect an error from chromeShot, observe nil
candidates.evidence: --- FAIL: TestChromeShotFalseSuccess/stale_file (0.00s) — "chromeShot returned nil after the browser wrote nothing, because a file from an earlier run was still at the destination"

candidates.summary: a URL the preview server answers 404 on is photographed and published as the realm's rendering, because chromeShot treats any non-empty PNG as a successful shot
candidates.failure_scenario: chromeShot(bin, origin+"/"+afterFile, dst) against a path that is not on disk returns nil and writes a 6743-byte PNG of the file server's "404 page not found" text. ScreenshotPairs then sets pair.After and the comment captions that error page as the realm, with nothing on stderr. Today every afterFile comes from c.pages, whose pages writePages has written, so the miss is latent rather than live; it becomes live the moment a page's file name and its served path stop agreeing (a prefix, an escape, a writeFile that failed).
candidates.verify_by: go test -run TestChromeShotFalseSuccess/missing_page ./... in misc/gnopreview with the artifact test: expect an error from chromeShot on a 404 URL, observe nil and a written PNG
candidates.evidence: --- FAIL: TestChromeShotFalseSuccess/missing_page (0.40s) — "chromeShot on a URL the server answers 404 on returned nil and wrote 6743 bytes"

candidates.summary: the screenshot server's Serve error is dropped, so a server that never starts is reported as a Chrome failure on every shot
candidates.failure_scenario: serve() backgrounds srv.Serve(ln) with the error discarded. If Serve returns before any Close — the listener refused, the handler panicking the goroutine away — every following chromeShot gets a connection error from the browser and prints "! screenshot <realm> (after): exit status 1", pointing the reader at Chrome while the failure was the local server. The //nolint reason, "Serve always returns on Close", covers only the shutdown case.
candidates.verify_by: read shots.go:153-164: no channel, no variable and no stderr write receives the value srv.Serve returns

dropped.summary: --virtual-time-budget=4000 is a no-op on current Chrome stable, so the frame is grabbed before the controller modules and webfonts the comment names have settled
dropped.settled_by: a package test calling chromeShot against a page whose div turns red on a 1200ms setTimeout: pixel(10,10)=255,0,0 after 400ms of wall clock, so virtual time did advance past the timer. A bare `google-chrome-stable --headless=new --virtual-time-budget=4000 --screenshot=...` against the same page behind `python3 -m http.server` stayed white, which is that single-threaded server holding a pending fetch and pausing virtual time, not the flag being ignored.
